_comment: Halo settings. Open them in a window with `halo settings`, or edit this file with `halo config edit`. Halo re-reads this file within a second of a change -- a hotkey change rebinds as soon as dictation is idle, everything else applies to the next thing you say. The vocabulary files beside this one (dictionary/snippets/commands) reload the same way. Any value here can be overridden for one run with an environment variable: HALO_HOTKEY, HALO_ACTIVATION, HALO_LANGUAGE, HALO_MODEL, HALO_THREADS, HALO_OVERLAY, HALO_PRIVACY, HALO_WHISPER_BIN.
_comment_activation: 'hold' = press and hold to talk, release to send. 'toggle' = one press starts, the next press sends, and Escape throws the clip away. Hold is the default because it cannot leave the microphone open; toggle is for long dictation, and max_recording_sec is its backstop.
_comment_whisper_bin: Absolute path to whisper-cli, filled in by `halo setup`. Leave empty to search PATH and the usual Homebrew prefixes -- but note launchd gives the background agent a bare PATH, so the absolute path is what makes it work at login.
_comment_menu_bar: Off by default. The hotkey is meant to be the whole interface, and `halo settings` reaches the Settings window without spending a slot in your menu bar.

orb._comment: The floating orb. 'scale' multiplies its 84pt bubble (0.6-1.6). 'position' is one of bottom, top, bottom-left, bottom-right, top-left, top-right, and 'inset' is the distance from that edge in points. Set show_while_processing to false and the orb vanishes the moment you stop speaking instead of staying up while Halo transcribes.

_comment_privacy: Privacy Mode at startup. On means the OpenRouter call is skipped entirely and only local processing runs. Saying 'privacy on' flips it at runtime and that choice persists.

dictation._comment: Local punctuation and formatting. All of this runs on this Mac with no key and no network, so it applies in Privacy Mode too. spoken_punctuation turns 'comma', 'new line' and 'question mark' into the marks they name; ambiguous words are left alone when they read as ordinary speech, so 'the Jurassic period was long' types as written.
dictation._comment_smart: Normal and Polished cleanup only. self_correction turns 'meet me Thursday, actually Friday' into 'meet me Friday'. smart_formatting writes numbers, dates, times, money, phone numbers, emails, URLs and spoken lists the way you would type them. chat_period keeps the final period on short chat messages, which chat apps otherwise skip.

whisper._comment: Decoder settings. The four numeric ones match whisper.cpp's own defaults and are pinned here so an upstream change cannot silently retune dictation. 'prompt' primes the decoder with your vocabulary and your previous utterance, which is the biggest accuracy win available without a larger model; turn it off only if you ever see your vocabulary list typed back at you.

cleanup._comment: How much Halo tidies what you said. 'mode' is off, verbatim, light, normal or polished. Normal and polished use a language model when one is available and fall back to the local rules the instant it is missing, loading, slow or wrong -- you never lose a dictation to it. 'provider' picks the model: auto (this Mac first, then OpenRouter), local, openrouter, or none for rules only. 'enabled' is your consent to send transcript text to OpenRouter at all; it needs a key (`halo key set`) and is skipped in Privacy Mode. The text around your cursor is never sent to OpenRouter. 'models' is the OpenRouter fallback chain, tried in order.

local._comment: The model on this Mac. 'llama.cpp' means Halo runs llama-server for you (`halo model local install` fetches the model). 'endpoint' means any OpenAI-compatible server already running on this Mac -- Ollama, LM Studio, mlx_lm.server -- given as 'endpoint' (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1) and 'endpoint_model'; addresses that are not this machine are refused. The budgets are hard ceilings in milliseconds.

context._comment: Context Awareness. When on, Halo looks at the app you are dictating into and a few hundred characters around the cursor -- in memory only, for that one dictation -- to get names, capitalization, spacing and formatting right. It never reads password or other secure fields, never writes that text to a log or to disk, and never sends it to OpenRouter. Dictation works the same with it off. 'app_overrides' maps an app's bundle id to chat, email, document, terminal, ide or browser.
